items_missed: Never asked 'how are you today?' — the customer asked Grant ('Hey grant, how you doing?') and Grant never returned it.

Agenda statement had the roadmap and the confirmation ('let me just walk you through how our pricing is gonna work and then I'll go over a rough estimate... Does that work for you?') but never gave the 10-15 minute timeframe, so it doesn't count as a true agenda opener.
Never probed additional rooms — no garage, attic, or storage-unit question, even though the customer volunteered two grills (a Blackstone and a Weber-type) that live outdoors or in a garage.
Never nailed the box count. Customer said '25 boxes' and then 'about twenty boxes' in the same breath; Grant let the contradiction stand and never confirmed a number.
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('Is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?').
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. Grant said 'insurance' was bundled in the hourly rate but never named the $2,000 per-move repair/replace/reimburse coverage or the 60 cents/lb baseline.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned — no email-before-the-move-with-your-mover's-photo pitch.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — no 'if we miss the window we start discounting immediately.'

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing. The customer teed it up perfectly ('we're starting the box up, put some stuff on the curve, getting rid of some stuff, given some stuff away') and Grant responded with 'Gotcha' instead of the prep-equals-lower-bill speech.
No 'take a carload' tip, no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, loose drawer items, photos off walls).
Stairs never explained as an estimate variable. The master bedroom — the single biggest room in the move — is on the second floor of the origin, and Grant never said stairs add time.
Specialty items not flagged as estimate variables: an 86-inch TV, a glass kitchen table, and a stainless refrigerator got a protection answer but no time impact.
Traffic not addressed as a variable even after the customer raised it directly ('about a thirty minute ride, I guess depending on how traffic is').
'No deposit required' never said — one of Einstein's two headline differentiators, omitted entirely.
Email mechanics not explained: no mention of the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email and no 'reply with any corrections' ask.
No final 'any other questions before I let you go?' — the call ended on walkthrough logistics.
Business hours and how to reach us never given.
No Ecobox referral, despite the customer needing roughly 20-25 boxes and actively decluttering.
top_strength: The pricing block was clean, confident, and complete on the mechanical side. Grant led with the exact scorecard opener — 'our pricing is super simple at the Garland branch' — then gave the rate per mover with the day tier ($105/hr per mover on Saturdays, $210/hr for a two-man team), itemized what's included (truck, gas, taxes, insurance, pads, wrap, bands, tools for disassembly/reassembly), and disclosed the $115 travel fee up front as the one exception rather than burying it. He also nailed all four clock bullets in a single tight passage: clock starts when the crew arrives on site and walks through with you, two-and-a-half hour minimum, fifteen-minute prorated increments after that, then a sense-check ('any questions about any of that info so far?'). His estimate framing was genuinely smart too — he translated a partial move out of a 2,600 sqft home into 'a one-ish bedroom equivalent coming out of a larger home,' gave a range (5.5 to 6.5 hours) with a dollar figure attached ($1,480 travel fee included), and reminded the customer he only pays for time actually worked past the minimum.
coaching_note: Grant, the single highest-leverage fix is the Save Your Ass speech, and this call is the textbook example of the money you leave on the table by skipping it. Kenneth handed you the opening on a platter — he told you he's already boxing, putting things on the curb, and giving stuff away. That is the moment to say: 'Kenneth, everything you just described is exactly what saves you money. The clock is running the whole time we're there, so every box you have sealed and stacked by the front door, every loose item out of a drawer, every picture off the wall before we arrive is time off your bill. And anything small enough to fit in your car — lamps, hampers, the closet stuff — take a carload over yourself the night before. Does that make sense?' Ten points, thirty seconds, and it directly improves your estimate accuracy on move day. Second priority is your differentiator block: you said 'insurance' is included but never sold it. Say the words — 'No Worries Damage Coverage, up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damages' — and add Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee, which cost you six points here and are the two things competitors can't match. Third, and this one is nearly free: you never said 'no deposit required,' and you never asked 'anything else I can answer before I let you go?' Two sentences at the close. Fix the agenda opener the same way — you have the roadmap and the 'does that work for you,' you're just missing 'takes about 10 to 15 minutes.' Add that one clause and you get the flag.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and unhurried language throughout ('Gotcha, no problem at all', 'Nice', 'no worries', 'Of course, you're very welcome, Kenneth'), used the customer's name four separate times including a respectful 'Mister Kenneth', and handled the Tiffany/Nevada address confusion patiently rather than correcting him flatly — the customer closed with unprompted appreciation ('thank you so much and I appreciate it').
